voyage.name: Sofia History Museum
voyage.content: Museum of the history of Sofia itself, housed in the colourful old building of the Central Mineral [Water] Baths (built 1913). Exhibits include many luxurious items formerly belonging to Bulgaria's last monarchs.

voyage.name: National Museum of Military History
voyage.content: The only museum in Bulgaria with 4 types of exhibitions – open air, chronological, collections and temporary exhibitions. Over 28 000 exhibits, dated from the Antiquity to the present day. The largest open air exhibition on the Balkans with over 300 pieces of military equipment. The richest collections of weapons, uniforms, decorations, art works, flags, photographs, military equipment, etc.

voyage.name: Institute of Ethnology and Folklore Studies with Ethnographic Museum
voyage.content: Has a permanent collection of traditional Bulgarian costumes and a changing exhibition.

voyage.name: Earth and Man National Museum
voyage.content: A large mineralogical museum. In the main hall is the world's biggest collection of Giant Crystals, with dazzling jagged rocks the size of refrigerators.

voyage.name: National Museum of History
voyage.content: The National Museum of History in the Rezidentsia Boyana provide a comprehensive view on Bulgarian history from the prehistory to present, in as broad of a European context as possible. With more than 650,000 exhibits, it is one of the largest history museums on the Balkans, so be prepared to spend several hours. One main attraction are golden and silver mugs and jewellery from Thracian (around 4th century BC) and Ro

voyage.name: National Institute of Archaeology and Museum
National Museum of Natural History
voyage.content: Has four floors of everything from rocks and minerals to insects and stuffed bison. It is a nice way to spend a rainy afternoon.

voyage.name: The Red Flat
voyage.content: Half tour, half experience. Walk around a house setup like an old communist flat from the 1980s. You're allowed to touch and play with just about anything. There's an audio guide in English, Spanish and Bulgarian.

voyage.name: Museum of Paleontology and Historical Geology
Museum of Socialist Art
voyage.content: After the Soviet Union fell and Bulgaria moved on from communism, much of the country's communist artwork was eventually collected here. Outside the museum (and free to access) is a small park crammed with statues of notable communists, with every flavor of Lenin.

voyage.name: National Art Gallery
voyage.content: Has old Bulgarian art, icons, etc. Also includes collections of the former National Gallery for Foreign Art, which are exhibited along with the 19th- and 20th-century collections of the National Art Gallery at National Gallery Square 500 (Kvadrat 500 in Bulgarian), which is at 1, 19th February St., St Alexander Nevsky Sq. and is open Tu-Su 10:00-18:00 and closed Mondays and holidays.

voyage.name: Sofia City Art Gallery
voyage.price: free entrance every second and fourth Thursday

voyage.name: St. Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
voyage.content: The largest church in the Balkans, and one of the largest Christian churches worldwide, able to hold 5,000 worshipers. Saint Alexander Nevsky was a Russian prince, and the cathedral was built to honour the Russian soldiers who died during the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878, liberating Bulgaria from Ottoman rule.

voyage.name: St. Sophia Church
voyage.content: It was built in the 6th century, in the same wave of construction as the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. In 1329 it gave its name to the city. It was destroyed several times and during the Ottoman rule it was used as a mosque. It was built over an even older 4th-century church, which can be explored through its excavated crypts and tombs.

voyage.name: Boyana Church
voyage.content: This small 11th-century church and garden is on the UNESCO World Heritage List for its well-preserved murals. The layer of fresco from 1259 shows realism and emotion evocative of the early Renaissance, but painted a century earlier. No photos are allowed inside, as the interior is dark and cramped. There is little interpretive information inside; you can hire an on-site tour guide or ask questions to the docent. Only

voyage.name: Catholic cathedral St. Joseph
voyage.content: Holy Masses: Sa 17:30 & Su 10:30 in Bulgarian; 12:00 in Latin; 18:00 Bulgarian

voyage.name: Banya Bashi Mosque
voyage.content: Beautiful yet simple Ottoman-mosque. Built by Mimar Sinan. It's active and there is a guide inside.

voyage.name: Sofia Synagogue
voyage.content: One of the largest in Europe.

voyage.name: Battenberg Mausoleum
voyage.content: The mausoleum and final resting place of Prince Alexander I of Bulgaria (1857–1893), the first Head of State of modern Bulgaria.

voyage.name: Monument to Vasil Levski
voyage.content: It commemorates the hanging of Bulgarian national hero and major revolutionary figure Vasil Levski in the city on 18 February 1873.

voyage.name: Monument to the Tsar Liberator
voyage.content: Representing the power of freedom and across from it are the National Assembly and the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences.

voyage.name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier
voyage.content: Across from Alexander Nevsky cathedral; on the side of Hagia Sofia's Church.

voyage.name: Tsar Samuil Monument
voyage.content: A statue of the Bulgarian warlord and tsar Samuil, who ruled Bulgaria between 997 and 1014.

voyage.name: Russian Monument
voyage.content: An obelisk built by the Russians.

voyage.name: Largo
voyage.content: 3 buildings of Socialist Classicism architecture, around what was designed to be the city's representative centre. The buildings are Council of Ministers and the TSUM department store on the north side, the National Assembly (former Communist Party headquarters) with its iconic spire on the east side, the Presidential Administration (former Council of State) and the Balkan Hotel to the south side.

voyage.name: Prince Alexander of Battenberg Square
voyage.content: The largest square in Sofia. Includes the National Art Gallery.

voyage.name: Petko R. Slaveykov Square
voyage.content: A famous square, real Sofia center with a monument of writers father and son Slaveykov. It`s a biggest open-air book market in the Balkans.There are round benches and street musicians act very often.

voyage.name: Patriarh Evtimiy Square
voyage.content: A popular meeting place.

voyage.name: Borisova Gradina (Boris Garden)
voyage.content: The oldest and best known park in the city. Includes the Ariana Lake.

voyage.name: City Garden
voyage.content: It's the oldest and most central public garden, in existence since 1872.

voyage.name: Yuzhen Park (South Park)
voyage.content: A nice park in the south-east part of the city, although a bit too crowded on weekends. Vibrant with open area cafes, entertainment for children and grown-ups, and a few ponds with ducks.

voyage.name: Oborishte Park
voyage.content: A park near the center of the city with places to eat and drink.

voyage.name: Kambanite Park
voyage.content: A park with bells from every country in the world.

voyage.name: Orlov Most
voyage.content: A bridge over the Perlovska River near the centre of Sofia

voyage.name: Lavov Most
voyage.content: A bridge over the Vladayska River near the central train station.

voyage.name: Snail House
voyage.content: A five story residential building in the shape of a giant pastel-striped snail, complete with two antennae.

voyage.name: SS. Cyril and Methodius National Library
Sofia Bike Tour
voyage.content: Visit Sofia and the countryside around on a "free" bike tour, every day at 11:00 and 17:00. Note, for the ride you will need to rent a bicycle with the tour operators. And like always, the word "free" is a euphemism for "tips strongly appreciated". Also, this tour might in addition be a way to market their chargeable tours; always compare before committing to anything.

voyage.name: Playgrounds
voyage.content: If you're travelling with kids, they might love playgrounds. The "rich" one is in the park that holds Vasil Levski stadium (close to the corner with Orlov Most; there are actually two playgrounds close to this corner and you'd look for the one more inside the park).

voyage.name: Sofia Opera and Ballet
voyage.content: During summer, open air shows in the evenings are offered.

voyage.name: Arena Cinema
voyage.content: One of the biggest Bulgarian cinema multiplex. Cinemas in Sofia play all films except children's films in their original language with Bulgarian subtitles.

voyage.name: National Palace of Culture
voyage.content: The biggest congress center in the Balkans (a massive monolithic communist-style building). If asking for directions, ask for NDK (en-de-ka), as most Bulgarians refer to it by this acronym.

voyage.name: Central Military Club
voyage.content: It`s a multi-purpose monument of culture building in the city center. Also known under the name Kristal.

voyage.name: Vitosha Boulevard
voyage.content: It`s the main commercial street in the centre of Sofia. Its pedestrian part is a popular place for walks. It is known as the most expensive street in Sofia.

voyage.name: The Mall
voyage.content: Largest shopping mall in Bulgaria; contains also a Carrefour store, large Arena cinema, a lot of cafes and restaurants, etc.

voyage.name: Central Sofia Market Hall
voyage.content: Has many stalls selling all kinds of food, drink and cosmetics. The second floor has various fast-food cafés. As of early 2023 closed for renovations..

voyage.name: Mall of Sofia
voyage.content: Contains a Piccadilly store and a Cinema City multiplex.

voyage.name: SkyCity Mall
voyage.content: Also has an entertainment centre.

voyage.name: Serdika Center Sofia
voyage.content: Contains a Piccadilly store.

voyage.name: Paradise Center
voyage.content: Largest shopping mall in Bulgaria; contains also a Carrefour store, large Arena cinema, a lot of cafes and restaurants, etc.

voyage.name: Sofia Ring Mall
voyage.content: Contains a karting track and a Cinema City multiplex.

voyage.name: Veselata Gozba Restaurant
voyage.content: Good variety of main courses, soups, salads and desserts. The food is delicious. Family-operated restaurant

voyage.name: Gastrobar 6
voyage.content: Favorite place for delicious food in a great pleasant atmosphere. You feel at home

voyage.name: Ali Baba
voyage.content: Good place for a quick bit of kebabs and falafel.

voyage.name: Dream House
voyage.content: Very good vegetarian restaurant. Quick service, simple and good food, good value for money.

voyage.name: Мекица и Кафе (Mekitsa and Coffee)
voyage.content: Here you can have brunch and the typical Bulgarian breakfast. One of them gems of Sofia. Great, hot, fresh, on the spot mekitsa. With very friendly staff. You can go to the second floor, sit at the table against the window, munch mekitsa and sip your beverage. Good times!

voyage.name: DARO
voyage.content: A breakfast restaurant

voyage.name: Pizza Victoria
voyage.content: One of the best Bulgarian pizzas.

voyage.name: Godzila
voyage.content: Godzila's first restaurant opened in 1999 in the sea capital of Bulgaria, Varna. Offers fresh salads, juicy barbecue, delicious pizza and various other dishes. Menus are in English and the staff speak English as well. There are traditional Bulgarian cuisine and Western cuisine as well.

voyage.name: Pod Lipite
voyage.content: Very good traditional food. Reservation is required.

voyage.name: Motto
voyage.content: This place is always fairly busy with a trendy crowd. The decor is modern and cool, and the people typically good looking. The service is usually good, and many of the staff speak English. The food is consistent and enjoyable.

voyage.name: Hadjidraganovite kashti
voyage.content: Amazing restaurant just off one of Sofia's main streets. The decor is old-style Bulgarian and the food is traditional Bulgarian, plentiful and very, very tasty. Entertainment includes a Bulgarian walking band and guests are primarily locals. Staff are very friendly and most speak English. Reservations are necessary, even on weeknights.

voyage.name: The Cocktail Bar
voyage.content: Tasty cocktails, crowded in the evenings, has a summer garden (it is actually in a small park, which becomes occupied by the customers)

voyage.name: Bar 5L
voyage.content: Speakeasy (5L is a transliteration of rooster in Bulgarian). Designer cocktails in cozy atmosphere. The key, corresponding to the day of the month, unlocks the door (not sure whether they change it at midnight).

voyage.name: Apartment
voyage.content: Popular among locals and foreigners is the "apartamenta", some sort of private club in the second floor of a turn of the 19th-century mansion where you find a series of rooms, all in different styles and wall-drawings, colourful tapestries, etc. Go to the right, get a drink in the kitchen, and just pick and choose a room which looks cozy enough (shouldn't be too hard to find one with all the couches lying around). If

voyage.name: 4km
voyage.price: Entrance is ~€10, but slightly cheaper if you arrive before midnight
voyage.content: This place plays mostly drum&bass and dubstep music.

voyage.name: Peter Pan Hostel
voyage.content: Owner-run, small hostel on the first floor of apartment building. Newly renovated. Small but clean rooms with single beds or bunk beds. Rooms come with TV, small balcony, fridge. Wifi available. No communal space or kitchen (only microwave).

voyage.name: Levitt Hostel
voyage.content: Offers free unlimited high speed Internet (1000 Mbit/s) and Wi-Fi connection through the entire hostel, free coffee and tea any time of the day, free use of fully equipped kitchen, free blankets, pillows and sheets, free towels on request, free laundry (with 3 nights stay), free use of iron/ironing board, free hair dryer, free city maps, travel desk, security system + 24 hours video surveillance, designated smoking a

voyage.name: Crosspoint Sofia Hostel
voyage.content: A hostel with a friendly atmosphere. Free Wi-Fi; 1-m-wide spacious and very comfortable beds; metal lockers. Offers mixed and female dorms as well as private rooms. Great young staff with an attitude working there.

voyage.name: Hostel Mostel
voyage.content: Beautiful wooden flooring. Has a huge lounge to chill out, you can browse the net on modern computers. Some dorm rooms are en-suite, trips to Rila Monastery are run daily. €5 for breakfast.

voyage.name: Nightingale Hostel
voyage.content: At Famous Slaveykov Square (center of the downtown), a non-smoking eco hostel provides beds and rooms and it is a social place with air-conditioning, common/TV room and lobby area. Free of charge- breakfast, kitchen, PC and WiFi internet, lockers, maps, call a taxi, book a club, check timetables service, hot showers in renovated and sexes separated toilets and 24-hr reception desk. Laundry, pick up, meals and drinks

voyage.name: Orient Express Hostel - Sofia
voyage.content: This small hostel offers a variety of room options.

voyage.name: Interhost / Hello Sofia
voyage.content: Formerly known as "Internet Hostel". Small place but very central. 3 (dorm) rooms, 1 apartment available in this location. Communal space: Small kitchen/dining area. No reception or staff on site, so announce your arrival upfront. Heating in the rooms is remote-controlled and only switched on at night times. The company operates several venues in Sofia. If you book in advance they might move you to a different locati

voyage.name: Alegra Hostel
voyage.content: VIBER: 00359889446364 Location:in the centre, at a quiet street, on the first floor of a three-storey residential building, with fully independent separate entrance and a tiny courtyard. The living area occupies 80 m². 4 separate rooms, individual locks, a fully equipped kitchen (kitchen stove, dishwasher, pots, saucepans, refrigerator, porcelain food sets, coffee machine, tea, microwave oven), two bathrooms with toi

voyage.name: 10 Coins Hostel
voyage.content: Average but friendly hostel outside of the centre, Small kitchen, quiet neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Sofia
voyage.content: Modern five-star hotel offering conference facilities and spa centre.

voyage.name: Holiday Village Diplomat
voyage.content: Is near Vitosha mountain and 20 min away from the city centre. Spacious rooms, large park area and friendly staff.

voyage.name: Maxim Hotel
voyage.content: A hotel 5 min walking distance from the train/bus station and 5 min away in the opposite direction from downtown Sofia. It is a cute hotel with a nice bedroom and also a living/TV room, large private bathroom and includes breakfast buffet in the morning. Only negative is they do not have an elevator. Cost in slow season was €60 for 2 people, €50 for one person.

voyage.name: Metropolitan Hotel Sofia
voyage.content: Business 4-star hotel near airport, ideal for business and leisure.

voyage.name: Red House B&B
voyage.content: A charming B&B in the Red House cultural centre.

voyage.name: Hello Sofia Guesthouse
voyage.content: Just opened small and cozy guesthouse in the very center of Downtown, eco-friendly, offers individually designed en-suite rooms, also deluxe dormitories and studios, furnished and supplied with all natural materials and fabrics/linens, pillows by choice, free parking during the weekends, free WiFi, 40" LED HDTVs and individual PCs in some of the rooms!

voyage.name: Sofia Hotel Balkan, a Marriott Luxury Collection Hotel
voyage.content: Impressive 5-storey hotel, in classical design, houses 184 rooms, including 19 suites. All rooms are soundproof, with air condition control, direct dial phone, message alert, TV with satellite program, radio, mini bar.

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Sofia Hotel
voyage.content: Set in a building that resembles a baroque castle, this hotel offers 77 rooms and 36 one- or two-bedroom apartments.
